# dsh-text-color-adaptive
Recolors DSH label text from the actual brightness of whatever is behind it, so white text on a brig
ht wallpaper stops washing out.
Built for the transparent-glass look (a wallpaper plus semi-transparent panels): the shipped dark-th
eme text color is a fixed near-white, and a live wallpaper keeps moving bright frames underneath it.
This plugin measures that backdrop and picks a side — light text or dark text — instead of assuming
plugin measures that backdrop and picks a side — light text or dark text — instead of assuming one.
## What it does
Every 0.9 s it samples the wallpaper layer (`.we-layer`, produced by dsh-plugin-wallpaper-engine) —
an ``, `
The frame is scaled to 64×36, the text column is averaged into one background color, and that color
is blended with the active theme's glass surface to estimate what the glyphs actually sit on. It the
n picks the side with the higher contrast and pushes the color until it just clears 4.6:1.
It writes five tokens — `--dsw-alias-label-primary`, `-secondary`, `-tertiary`, `-caption`, `-dimmed
` — plus a text shadow that runs opposite to the text color (dark text gets a light shadow and vice
versa) as a safety net.
Switching sides is damped: the new side has to beat the current one by 1.15× on two consecutive samp
les, so a live wallpaper does not flicker.
## When it cannot sample
No wallpaper layer, a frame that is not decoded yet, or a scene iframe that refuses `__wp.capture()`
(cross-origin) — the plugin turns itself off completely (removes `html[data-at-adaptive]`) and leav
es DSH's own colors untouched. It never leaves half an override behind.
Without the wallpaper plugin there is nothing to sample, and DSH's solid background needs no help; t
he plugin stays dormant.
